import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 7.23

by A. V. Kuznetsov

Does there exist an algorithm which decides, for a given finite list of group identities, whether
the variety defined by the list is abelian? By a theorem of A. P. Zamyatin, this is equivalent to
asking whether the elementary theory of the variety is decidable.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«7.23»

/--
Does there exist an algorithm deciding whether the variety defined by a finite list of group
identities is abelian?

A group word in countably many variables is encoded by a list of pairs in `ℕ × Bool`, and an
identity is a pair of words. A group belongs to the variety when, under every assignment of the
variables to its elements, the two words in every listed identity have equal values.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«7.23» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ComputablePred fun identities : List (List (ℕ × Bool) × List (ℕ × Bool)) =>
      ∀ (G : Type) [Group G],
        (∀ identity ∈ identities, ∀ f : ℕ → G,
          FreeGroup.lift f (FreeGroup.mk identity.1) =
            FreeGroup.lift f (FreeGroup.mk identity.2)) →
        ∀ x y : G, x * y = y * x := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«7.23»
modeling_decisions: Encoded a group word effectively as `List (ℕ × Bool)`, where the natural number names one of countably many variables and the Boolean records the exponent sign; encoded an identity as a pair of words and the finite input as a `List` of such pairs.
Interpreted words using Mathlib's `FreeGroup.mk` followed by `FreeGroup.lift`, so satisfaction means equality under every assignment of variables in every group.

Expressed that the generated variety is abelian by requiring pairwise commutativity in every group satisfying every listed identity. Used this abelian reformulation as the predicate passed to `ComputablePred`, in accordance with the statement's citation of Zamyatin.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 7.23

by A. V. Kuznetsov

Does there exist an algorithm which decides, for a given list of group identities,
whether the elementary theory of the variety given by this list is soluble
(i.e. decidable), that is, by A. P. Zamyatin (*Algebra and Logic* **17**, no. 1 (1978),
13–17), whether this variety is abelian?

Zamyatin proved that a variety of groups has a decidable elementary theory if and
only if it is abelian, so the problem asks whether the set of finite lists of group
identities defining an abelian variety is decidable.

A group identity (law) is written as $w = 1$, where $w$ is a word in the free group
on the countably many variables $x_0, x_1, \dots$; an identity $u = v$ is the same
as $u v^{-1} = 1$. A group $G$ satisfies $w = 1$ if $w$ evaluates to $1$ under every
assignment of elements of $G$ to the variables. The variety given by a list of
identities is the class of all groups satisfying every identity in the list, and it
is abelian if every group in it is commutative.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«7.23»

/-- A group word in the variables $x_0, x_1, \dots$, given as a list of letters
`(i, b)`, where `(i, true)` stands for $x_i$ and `(i, false)` for $x_i^{-1}$.
This is the input format of `FreeGroup.mk`, so `FreeGroup.mk w` is the element
of the free group `FreeGroup ℕ` represented by `w`. -/
abbrev GroupWord : Type := List (ℕ × Bool)

/-- A group `G` satisfies the identity $w = 1$ if $w$ evaluates to $1$ under every
assignment `f` of elements of `G` to the variables. -/
def SatisfiesIdentity (G : Type*) [Group G] (w : GroupWord) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : ℕ → G, FreeGroup.lift f (FreeGroup.mk w) = 1

/-- The variety of groups given by the list of identities `L` (the class of all groups
satisfying every identity in `L`) is abelian: every group satisfying all identities
in `L` is commutative. -/
def IsAbelianVariety (L : List GroupWord) : Prop :=
  ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], (∀ w ∈ L, SatisfiesIdentity G w) → IsMulCommutative G

/--
Does there exist an algorithm which decides, for a given (finite) list of group
identities $w_1 = 1, \dots, w_n = 1$, whether the elementary theory of the variety
given by this list is soluble (i.e. decidable), that is, by Zamyatin's theorem,
whether this variety is abelian?

Formally: is the predicate "the variety given by `L` is abelian" a computable
predicate on finite lists `L` of group words?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3 20]
theorem kourovka.«7.23» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ComputablePred fun L : List GroupWord => IsAbelianVariety L := by
  sorry

/-- The empty list of identities gives the variety of all groups, which is not
abelian. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem not_isAbelianVariety_nil : ¬ IsAbelianVariety [] := by
  intro h
  have := h (Equiv.Perm (Fin 3)) (by simp)
  exact absurd (this.is_comm.comm (Equiv.swap 0 1) (Equiv.swap 1 2)) (by decide)

/-- The single identity $x_0 x_1 x_0^{-1} x_1^{-1} = 1$ gives the variety of abelian
groups. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isAbelianVariety_commutator :
    IsAbelianVariety [[(0, true), (1, true), (0, false), (1, false)]] := by
  intro G _ h
  refine ⟨⟨fun a b => ?_⟩⟩
  have := h _ (List.mem_singleton_self _) (fun n => if n = 0 then a else b)
  simp [FreeGroup.lift_mk] at this
  rw [← mul_assoc, ← mul_assoc, mul_inv_eq_one, mul_inv_eq_iff_eq_mul] at this
  exact this

end Kourovka.«7.23»
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The single-slot decomposition is right: the "that is, … abelian" clause is the notebook's own reformulation via Zamyatin's theorem, so the formalized Prop is decidability of "the variety given by the list is abelian".
modeling_decisions: Group identities are represented as single words w (meaning the law w = 1) rather than pairs u = v; the two formats are trivially computably inter-translatable (u = v iff u v⁻¹ = 1), so decidability is unaffected. Documented in the module docstring.

Words are encoded concretely as `List (ℕ × Bool)` (the input format of `FreeGroup.mk`), because `ComputablePred` needs a `Primcodable` input type and `FreeGroup ℕ` has none. Different lists may represent the same free-group element, but `SatisfiesIdentity` only depends on `FreeGroup.mk w`, and decidability on lists is equivalent to decidability on reduced words since reduction is computable.
Variables are indexed by ℕ (countably many), matching the standard setting of group varieties; a finite list of words only uses finitely many of them.

`IsAbelianVariety L` quantifies over groups in `Type` only (a theorem statement cannot quantify over all universes). This is equivalent to the universe-polymorphic reading: if all groups in `Type` satisfying `L` are commutative then the relatively free group `FreeGroup ℕ ⧸ (verbal subgroup of L)` (which lives in `Type`) is commutative, so the commutator law follows from `L` and every group in any universe satisfying `L` is commutative.
Commutativity is expressed via Mathlib's `IsMulCommutative G` class, following existing Kourovka files (e.g. 20_76.lean).

'Soluble' in the statement is read as 'decidable' (algorithmically solvable elementary theory), per Zamyatin's theorem; the abelian reformulation is the formalized Prop, as the decomposition table instructs.
The trivial variety (e.g. list containing the word x₀) counts as abelian under this definition, which agrees with Zamyatin's theorem (the trivial variety has a decidable elementary theory).

/-!
# Conjecture 7.23

by A. V. Kuznetsov

Does there exist an algorithm which decides, for a given list of group identities,
whether the elementary theory of the variety given by this list is soluble (decidable),
that is, by A. P. Zamyatin (*Algebra and Logic* **17**, no. 1 (1978), 13–17), whether
this variety is abelian?

A group identity is an equation $u = v$ between two words in the free group on the
countably many generators $x_0, x_1, \dots$. A group $G$ satisfies it if every
substitution of elements of $G$ for the generators makes $u$ and $v$ equal. The variety
given by a list of identities is the class of all groups satisfying every identity in
the list; it is abelian if all these groups are commutative.

By Zamyatin's theorem the elementary theory of a variety of groups is decidable if and
only if the variety is abelian, so the question asks whether the set of finite lists of
identities defining an abelian variety is decidable.

Words are encoded as lists of letters `(i, true)` (the generator $x_i$) and
`(i, false)` (its inverse $x_i^{-1}$), and are read in the free group via `FreeGroup.mk`.
This makes a list of identities finite data, so that `ComputablePred` applies.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«7.23»

/-- A word in the generators $x_0, x_1, \dots$ of the free group on countably many
generators, given as a list of letters: `(i, true)` stands for $x_i$ and `(i, false)`
stands for $x_i^{-1}$. It is read in `FreeGroup ℕ` via `FreeGroup.mk`. -/
abbrev GroupWord : Type := List (ℕ × Bool)

/-- A group identity $u = v$, given by a pair of words `(u, v)`. -/
abbrev GroupIdentity : Type := GroupWord × GroupWord

/-- A group `G` satisfies the identity $u = v$ if every substitution $x_i \mapsto f(i)$ of
elements of `G` for the generators makes $u$ and $v$ equal in `G`. -/
def SatisfiesIdentity (G : Type*) [Group G] (w : GroupIdentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : ℕ → G, FreeGroup.lift f (FreeGroup.mk w.1) = FreeGroup.lift f (FreeGroup.mk w.2)

/-- The variety of groups given by the list of identities `L` is abelian: every group
satisfying all the identities in `L` is commutative. -/
def IsAbelianVariety (L : List GroupIdentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], (∀ w ∈ L, SatisfiesIdentity G w) → IsMulCommutative G

/--
Does there exist an algorithm which decides, for a given (finite) list of group
identities, whether the elementary theory of the variety given by this list is
decidable, that is, by Zamyatin's theorem, whether this variety is abelian?

Formally: is the set of finite lists of group identities whose variety is abelian a
decidable (recursive) set?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3 20]
theorem kourovka.«7.23» : answer(sorry) ↔ ComputablePred IsAbelianVariety := by
  sorry

/-- Every group satisfies the trivial identity $w = w$. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem satisfiesIdentity_refl (G : Type*) [Group G] (w : GroupWord) :
    SatisfiesIdentity G (w, w) :=
  fun _ => rfl

/-- The identity $x_0 x_1 = x_1 x_0$ holds in a group iff the group is commutative. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem satisfiesIdentity_comm_iff (G : Type*) [Group G] :
    SatisfiesIdentity G ([(0, true), (1, true)], [(1, true), (0, true)]) ↔
      IsMulCommutative G := by
  simp only [SatisfiesIdentity, FreeGroup.lift_mk, List.map_cons, List.map_nil, cond_true,
    List.prod_cons, List.prod_nil, mul_one]
  refine ⟨fun h => ⟨⟨fun a b => ?_⟩⟩, fun h f => h.is_comm.comm _ _⟩
  exact h (fun i => if i = 0 then a else b)

/-- The variety given by the single identity $x_0 x_1 = x_1 x_0$ is abelian. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isAbelianVariety_comm :
    IsAbelianVariety [([(0, true), (1, true)], [(1, true), (0, true)])] :=
  fun G _ h => (satisfiesIdentity_comm_iff G).1 (h _ (List.mem_singleton_self _))

/-- The variety given by the empty list of identities (the variety of all groups) is not
abelian. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem not_isAbelianVariety_nil : ¬ IsAbelianVariety [] := by
  intro h
  have := (h (Equiv.Perm (Fin 3)) (by simp)).is_comm.comm (Equiv.swap 0 1) (Equiv.swap 1 2)
  exact absurd this (by decide)

end Kourovka.«7.23»
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The single-slot decomposition and its note (abelian form as the stated Prop, 'soluble' = decidable, finite input list) match my reading of the statement.
modeling_decisions: Group identities are modelled as pairs of words `(u, v)` meaning `u = v` (a law `w = 1` is the special case `(w, [])`). Words are lists of letters `(i, true)` = xᵢ and `(i, false)` = xᵢ⁻¹ in the free group on ℕ-indexed generators, interpreted through `FreeGroup.mk`; this concrete encoding is what makes the input `Primcodable`. Any other reasonable computable encoding yields an equivalent decidability question.
`SatisfiesIdentity G (u, v)` quantifies over all assignments `f : ℕ → G` and uses `FreeGroup.lift f`; this is equivalent to quantifying over all homomorphisms `FreeGroup ℕ →* G`.

`IsAbelianVariety` quantifies over groups `G : Type` (universe 0), following the other Kourovka files. This is harmless: a non-abelian group in the variety contains a 2-generated (countable) non-abelian subgroup, which also satisfies the identities and is isomorphic to a group in `Type`.

'Soluble' (разрешима) is read as 'algorithmically decidable', and the abelian form (via Zamyatin's 1978 theorem) is the stated Prop as fixed by the decomposition table; the elementary-theory-decidability version is not separately formalized.
Decidability is expressed with Mathlib's `ComputablePred` (existence of a decision procedure / recursive set), the same idiom used in `FormalConjectures/Paper/BranchingVAS.lean`.

Four short proved `@[category test]` theorems check the bespoke definitions: reflexive identities hold in every group; the identity x₀x₁ = x₁x₀ holds iff the group is commutative; the variety of that identity is abelian; the variety of the empty list (all groups) is not abelian.

/-!
# Conjecture 7.23

by A. V. Kuznetsov

Does there exist an algorithm which decides, for a given list of group identities, whether the
elementary theory of the variety given by this list is soluble (i.e. decidable), that is, by
Zamyatin's theorem, whether this variety is abelian?

A group identity is an equation $u = v$ between two words in the letters $x_i^{\pm 1}$,
$i \in \mathbb{N}$. A group $G$ satisfies the identity if $u$ and $v$ take the same value under
every assignment of the variables $x_i$ to elements of $G$. The variety given by a list of
identities is the class of all groups satisfying every identity in the list. This variety is
abelian if every group in it is abelian.

By A. P. Zamyatin (*Algebra and Logic* **17** (1978), 13–17), the elementary theory of a variety
of groups is decidable if and only if the variety is abelian. The problem therefore asks whether
the set of finite lists of group identities whose variety is abelian is decidable.

*References:*
- [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46), problem 7.23
- A. P. Zamyatin, *A non-Abelian variety of groups has an undecidable elementary theory*,
  Algebra and Logic **17** (1978), 13–17.
-/

namespace Kourovka.«7.23»

/-- A group word in the letters $x_i^{\pm 1}$, $i \in \mathbb{N}$: a list of pairs
`(i, b)`, where `(i, true)` stands for $x_i$ and `(i, false)` stands for $x_i^{-1}$. -/
abbrev GroupWord := List (ℕ × Bool)

/-- A group identity $u = v$, given by a pair of group words $(u, v)$. -/
abbrev GroupIdentity := GroupWord × GroupWord

/-- The value of a group word `w` in a group `G` under the assignment `f` of the
variables $x_i$ to elements of `G`. -/
def GroupWord.eval {G : Type*} [Group G] (f : ℕ → G) (w : GroupWord) : G :=
  FreeGroup.lift f (FreeGroup.mk w)

/-- A group `G` satisfies the identity $u = v$ if $u$ and $v$ take the same value in `G`
under every assignment of the variables $x_i$ to elements of `G`. -/
def SatisfiesIdentity (G : Type*) [Group G] (e : GroupIdentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : ℕ → G, e.1.eval f = e.2.eval f

/-- The variety of groups given by the list of identities `L` is abelian: every group
satisfying all the identities in `L` is abelian. -/
def IsAbelianVariety (L : List GroupIdentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], (∀ e ∈ L, SatisfiesIdentity G e) → IsMulCommutative G

/--
Does there exist an algorithm which decides, for a given list of group identities, whether the
elementary theory of the variety given by this list is soluble (i.e. decidable), that is, by
Zamyatin's theorem (*Algebra and Logic* **17** (1978), 13–17), whether this variety is abelian?

Here an identity $u = v$ is encoded as a pair of words in the letters $x_i^{\pm 1}$, and a
(finite) list of identities is an element of `List GroupIdentity`. The variety given by the
list is abelian if every group satisfying all the identities in the list is abelian. The
existence of the algorithm is expressed by `ComputablePred`.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3 20]
theorem kourovka.«7.23» : answer(sorry) ↔ ComputablePred IsAbelianVariety := by
  sorry

/-- The value of a group word is the product of the values of its letters. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem GroupWord.eval_eq_prod {G : Type*} [Group G] (f : ℕ → G) (w : GroupWord) :
    w.eval f = (w.map fun x => cond x.2 (f x.1) (f x.1)⁻¹).prod :=
  FreeGroup.lift_mk

/-- The variety given by the single commutator identity $x_0 x_1 x_0^{-1} x_1^{-1} = 1$
is abelian. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isAbelianVariety_commutator :
    IsAbelianVariety [([(0, true), (1, true), (0, false), (1, false)], [])] := by
  intro G _ hG
  refine ⟨⟨fun x y => ?_⟩⟩
  have h := hG _ (List.mem_singleton_self _) fun i => if i = 0 then x else y
  simp [GroupWord.eval_eq_prod] at h
  rwa [← mul_assoc, ← mul_assoc, mul_inv_eq_one, mul_inv_eq_iff_eq_mul] at h

/-- The variety of all groups, given by the empty list of identities, is not abelian. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem not_isAbelianVariety_nil : ¬ IsAbelianVariety [] := by
  intro h
  have := h (Equiv.Perm (Fin 3)) (by simp)
  exact absurd (this.is_comm.comm (Equiv.swap 0 1) (Equiv.swap 1 2)) (by decide)

end Kourovka.«7.23»

'Soluble' is read as 'algorithmically decidable' (the standard Russian-to-English rendering), and the algorithm's existence is expressed by Mathlib's `ComputablePred` (existence of a computable decision function).

A group identity is encoded as a pair (u, v) of words, each word being a `List (ℕ × Bool)` with `(i, true)` = x_i and `(i, false)` = x_i⁻¹; a finite list of identities is a `List` of such pairs.
